clue.text: Ached badly in cold season? Get a jacket

indicators.note: in says the scrambled letters sit inside the season word

parts.note: winter is the cold season

indicators.note: done badly, the letters of ached are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone aching through the winter is told to buy a coat.
explanation.definitionFit: A windproof outer garment is a kind of short coat or jacket.

clue.text: Some hospital garments in these cupboards?

parts.note: a ward is a room or section of a hospital
robes are long loose garments

explanation.surface: Asks whether hospital clothing is kept in these storage units.
explanation.definitionFit: Tall storage units for hanging clothes are a type of cupboard.

clue.text: Last part of serenade we hear uttered in beastly fashion

indicators.note: we hear says the ending of the word is spoken, giving a sound-alike

parts.note: the final syllable of serenade is spelt nade

explanation.surface: The close of a love song is sung in an animal-like way.
explanation.walkthrough: The '-nade' ending of serenade is said like the horse's cry in the past tense.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse's cry is an animal noise, so a horse that made it spoke like a beast.

clue.text: Rain I care about — needed for plant

indicators.note: about here means moved around, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A gardener says that rain is what the plant needs.
explanation.definitionFit: Cineraria is a flowering garden plant of the daisy family.

clue.text: Do well with fish, catching ninety

indicators.note: catching means the fish word holds the number inside it

parts.note: an eel is a fish
XC is ninety in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: An angler succeeds by landing a fish that brings a score of ninety.
explanation.definitionFit: To shine or outperform is to do well.

clue.text: Take care, if lacking recipe, when cooking food

indicators.note: cooking means the remaining letters are mixed up
lacking says a letter is removed from the phrase

parts.note: R is the standard abbreviation for recipe (Latin recipe, take)

explanation.surface: A kitchen warning: be careful if cooking without a recipe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'if lacking' drops R from TAKE CARE, leaving TAKECAE, which 'when cooking' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweet bun usually toasted and buttered is a foodstuff, a general example.

clue.text: Engineers with computer technology meeting hospital broadcasting boss

parts.note: RE stands for Royal Engineers, the British army corps
IT is information technology
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: Technicians and IT staff meet a hospital's head of broadcasting.
explanation.walkthrough: John Reith was the first director-general of the BBC, Britain's public broadcaster.
explanation.definitionFit: Lord Reith ran the BBC in its early years, its founding chief.

clue.text: Like a type of dish with some vinegar — nice

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A dish dressed with a bit of vinegar sounds pleasant.
explanation.definitionFit: The French culinary term means garnished, describing dishes served with trimmings, as in bouquet garni.

clue.text: Female, 54, and an old rocker wandered in pursuit of pleasure

parts.note: a gal is an informal word for a girl or woman
LIV is 54 in Roman numerals
a Ted, or Teddy Boy, was a 1950s British rock-and-roll youth

explanation.surface: A woman of 54 and an ageing rock fan went out having fun.
explanation.walkthrough: Teddy Boys were a 1950s British youth cult tied to early rock and roll.
explanation.definitionFit: To gad about seeking amusement is exactly what the verb means.

clue.text: Fruit from exhibition centre obtained by sailor in East

parts.note: the NEC is the National Exhibition Centre in Birmingham
tar is an old word for a sailor
E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: Fruit brought to a trade show by a sailor out east.
explanation.definitionFit: A smooth-skinned variety of peach is a fruit.

clue.text: Poetic curse this Little Englander may contrive

indicators.note: contrive means to fashion something, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A narrow-minded patriot might compose a curse in verse.
explanation.definitionFit: A Little Englander is someone insular and hostile to Europe, an opponent of the EU.

clue.text: Attraction outside church — Rex the dog

indicators.note: outside says the attraction word wraps round the church abbreviation

parts.note: a lure is an attraction or enticement
R stands for Rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A dog named Rex is drawn to something by a church.
explanation.definitionFit: A crossbred hunting hound, often greyhound and collie, is a breed of dog.

clue.text: Deranged king keeping the strap for punishment?

indicators.note: keeping means the king's name holds the word inside it

parts.note: Shakespeare's King Lear goes mad

explanation.surface: A mad monarch holds on to the belt used for beatings.
explanation.definitionFit: A leather is a strap, and to leather someone is to thrash them, hence a punishment belt.

clue.text: This person's qualification to teach is put down

parts.note: the setter refers to themself, and this person is gives I am, I'm
BEd is a Bachelor of Education degree

explanation.surface: A teacher's teaching degree has been dismissed.
explanation.definitionFit: To embed, also spelt this way, is to set something firmly down into a surface.

clue.text: Men going over B&B by lake — the latest in senseless crimes

indicators.note: going over means the word is turned back on itself

parts.note: OR stands for other ranks, soldiers who are not officers
bed and breakfast, written as two Bs
Erie is one of the Great Lakes

indicators.note: the latest means the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: Soldiers visit a lakeside guesthouse in a pointless crime spree.
explanation.definitionFit: Thefts carried out by force or threat are crimes.

clue.text: Gambler in deterioration — so not this?

parts.note: a better is one who bets
food that has gone off is deteriorating

explanation.surface: A punter losing ground is plainly not in an improved position.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the rest of the clue: someone in decline is the opposite of in a happier state.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone in decline is not in an improved situation, the phrase meaning more prosperous.

clue.text: Nice soil's found loose in certain rocky areas

indicators.note: loose means the letters are set free and rearranged

explanation.surface: Pleasant soil is found loose in some stony districts.
explanation.definitionFit: In geology these are folds whose limbs dip at the same angle, a feature of rock formations.

clue.text: Shop worker is idiot and is ultimately incompetent worker

parts.note: an ass is a fool

indicators.note: ultimately points to the last letter of the word

parts.note: a worker ant is the stock crossword worker

explanation.surface: A sales clerk is a fool and a useless employee.
explanation.definitionFit: Shop staff who serve customers are called sales assistants.

clue.text: A bit of light paper and a piece of timber

parts.note: the Sun is a British tabloid newspaper
a beam is a long piece of timber

explanation.surface: A list of materials: a sliver of light, some paper and wood.
explanation.definitionFit: A ray from the sun is a single shaft of light.

clue.text: One got by Stephen? Maybe the one that killed him?

definitions.text: One got by Stephen? Maybe the one that killed him?

parts.words: One got by Stephen? Maybe the one that killed him?
parts.note: Saint Stephen, the first Christian martyr, was put to death by a crowd hurling rocks at him

explanation.surface: A puzzling question about what Stephen received and what killed him.
explanation.definitionFit: Saint Stephen was killed by being pelted with rocks, so each missile is one he received.

clue.text: A wish I conjured up to have Latin introduced as living language

indicators.note: introduced means the letter is put into the mix
conjured up means the letters are magicked into a new order

explanation.surface: A magician grants a wish by bringing in Latin as a spoken tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'conjured up' turns A WISH I into SWAHII; L goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bantu tongue of East Africa is still spoken today, unlike Latin.

clue.text: Bird lands on summit — it's hairy

indicators.note: lands on means the bird is placed on the summit word, following it

parts.note: the top is the summit
the knot is a wading bird

explanation.surface: A bird alights on a mountain peak, which is covered in growth.
explanation.definitionFit: A tuft of hair tied up on the crown of the head is made of hair.

clue.text: Was model contrary having lost initial work?

indicators.note: having lost initial means letters are dropped from the front of the word

parts.note: opposed means contrary
op, short for opus, is a musical work

explanation.surface: A sitter who was awkward lost their first modelling job.
explanation.definitionFit: To pose is to sit for an artist or photographer, so the past tense means acted as a model.

clue.text: Traffic to speed up going over end of village

indicators.note: going over says the first piece sits above the second in the down light
in a down clue, up means the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: to dart is to speed

indicators.note: end of means the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: Cars speed up as they pass the edge of a village.
explanation.definitionFit: Traffic as commerce, the dealing in goods, is a synonym for business exchange.

clue.text: English apostle and French American soldier may wear it

parts.note: Paul is an apostle
et is French for and

explanation.surface: An Englishman, an apostle and a Frenchman with a US soldier's kit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'American' signals the US spelling, with a single T and no -TE.
explanation.definitionFit: A shoulder ornament on a uniform is worn by soldiers, here spelt the US way.

clue.text: Criminal adored being punished, especially being locked up!

indicators.note: locked up means the abbreviation is shut inside the jumbled letters
being punished means the letters are knocked about

explanation.surface: A beloved outlaw is punished by being jailed.
explanation.definitionFit: A reckless outlaw of the Wild West is a kind of criminal.

clue.text: One getting on in charge of architectural style

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
taken as written

explanation.surface: An ageing person in charge of the building's design style.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the classical orders of columns, with scroll capitals, is an architectural style.

clue.text: Insects beginning to leap in new-style photos taken by mother

parts.note: a dam is the mother of an animal

indicators.note: in places the letter inside the photos word

parts.note: selfies are a modern kind of photograph

indicators.note: beginning to means the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A mother takes trendy pictures of bugs jumping.
explanation.definitionFit: Slender flying creatures related to dragonflies are insects.
